full_judgment: 3. The DCC (respondent Nos. 1-4) contested this Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter-alia, that the land in question of 52.36 acres was acquired by the WDB through LA Case No. 20/76-77 for the purpose of construction of embankment and after construction of the said embankment, the WDB handed over the said 52.36 acres of land to the DCC on 3-6-1989 and the land of Mouza-Mirpur CS Khatian No. 1106, SA Khatian No. 4, Dag No. 641 and 633 and also the lands of Mouza Mirpur CS Khatian No. 1106, S.A. Khatian No. 4, Dag No. 502 were acquired by the Roads and Highways Department under LA Case No. 32/88-89 and were handed over the same to the DCC on 2-10-1998. Regarding the advertisement for lease of the case-lands in the newspapers and receiving Salami, it is stated that the petitioners in collaboration with some corrupt officials of the DCC had attempted to enter into vague agreements, as there was no approval from the Government to lease out the case land to anybody. It is further stated that no allotment letter was issued to the petitioners and the DCC has never received any rent from the petitioners and, therefore, no contract or lease agreement was executed, no possessions have ever been handed over in favour of the petitioners and no rehabilitation programme for the writ petitioners was ever taken by the 15CC. On 2-2-2010, in the ECNEC meeting a project with the financial aid of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) for setting up a modern slaughtering house in the case land was approved and the period to complete the project was fixed to be December, 2010 but due to the order of status-qua passed by this Court in the instant Writ Petition, the DCC could not hand over the possession to the project office despite the repeated requests by the Ministry of Local Government. In the mean time, the time for completion of the project work has lapsed and there is a possibility to withdraw the grants for the project sanctioned by the ADB. The said project is very much needed for environment, health and economic development of the DCC and also to help make progress in achieving the millennium development goals (MDG).
